newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania force leads NATO to scrap Spanish exercise.
newsitem.headline: Albania force leads NATO to scrap Spanish exercise.

text.p: NATO said on Thursday it had cancelled a nine-nation military exercise due to have begun in Spain next week because some states had a clash of commitments, including participation in a United Nations-approved security force for Albania.

NATO's southern command said in a statement the amphibious training exercise, Destined Glory 97, would not go ahead after "several nations had withdrawn or reduced their participation... in order to meet national operational commitments".
A NATO spokeswoman said the planned multinational Albania force was one of the reasons why some could not take part.

Destined Glory 97 was to have been the first major NATO military exercise hosted by Spain, and had been set for April 7 to 20 with forces from France, Germany, Greece, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Turkey, Britain and the United States.

France, Greece, Turkey and Spain have said they will take part in a planned Italian-led multinational force which Rome hopes to start deploying next week to accompany humanitarian relief efforts in chaotic Albania.
NATO did not say if Destined Glory 97 would be rescheduled.
The Italian-led force to Albania has United Nations approval but is not being organised under U.N. or NATO auspices.

It is designed to secure airports, ports and transport routes to enable humanitarian aid to be sent to the country following armed anarchy last month in the wake of the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes.
